readme:
# Product Hunt Scraper

Read the Product Hunt leaderboard for any day, week or month. Give a date, and the actor returns the ranked products of that leaderboard: name, tagline, rank, votes, comments, topics, thumbnail, launch date and links. No login and no API key are needed.

## What you get

- One record per product on the leaderboard of each date you ask for.
- Daily, weekly or monthly leaderboards.
- Several dates in one run. Set `maxResults` and the actor stops when it has that many products.
- Each product once per run, even if it shows up on more than one page.
- Sponsored slots are left out. Only ranked products are returned.
- A run that is interrupted continues where it stopped. Products already delivered are not delivered or charged again.
- You pay only for products that were saved to the dataset.

## Use with AI agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client, such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain or LlamaIndex.

**MCP server URL:**

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/producthunt-scraper
```

**Example prompt once connected:**

> "Use `producthunt-scraper` to list the Product Hunt launches of 4 November 2026 with their votes and topics, as a table."

## Data extracted

| Field | Example |
|-------|---------|
| `id` | `"1295912"` |
| `slug` | `"wanaka-studio"` |
| `url` | `"https://www.producthunt.com/products/wanaka-studio"` |
| `name` | `"Wanaka Studio"` |
| `tagline` | `"Make and publish 3D games with the first AI game engine"` |
| `product_id`, `product_slug` | `"1359160"`, `"wanaka-studio"` |
| `rank` | `1` (the rank on the leaderboard that was read) |
| `daily_rank`, `weekly_rank`, `monthly_rank` | `1`, `2`, `4` |
| `votes_count` | `429` |
| `launch_day_votes` | `416` |
| `comments_count` | `106` |
| `topics`, `topic_slugs` | `["Artificial Intelligence", "Games"]` |
| `thumbnail_url` | Thumbnail image |
| `outbound_url` | Product Hunt link that leads to the product website |
| `featured` | `true` |
| `launch_date` | `"2026-11-04"` |
| `featured_at`, `scheduled_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at` | Timestamps as shown by the site |
| `product_state` | `"default"` |
| `featured_comment_text`, `featured_comment_author`, `featured_comment_author_url` | The featured comment, when the page shows one |
| `contest_name` | Contest name, when shown |
| `leaderboard_date` | `"2026-11-04"` |
| `leaderboard_mode` | `"daily"` |
| `source_url` | The leaderboard page the row came from |
| `data_source` | `"apollo"` |
| `scraped_at` | `"2026-11-06T08:00:00Z"` |

Fields that a page does not show are returned empty (null).

## Pricing

Pay-per-event pricing. You pay only for products that were saved to the dataset.

| Event | Price |
|-------|-------|
| Actor start (`actor-start`) | $0.001 per run |
| Product scraped (`producthunt-product-result`) | $0.001 per product ($1.00 per 1,000) |

The start event is charged once per run, together with the first saved product. A run that returns nothing is not charged. If you set a maximum cost per run, the actor stops before it goes over that limit.

## Input

| Field | Type | Description | Default |
|-------|------|-------------|---------|
| `mode` | string | `daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`. Weekly and monthly read the week or month that contains each date. | `daily` |
| `dates` | string[] | Dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Each date gives one leaderboard page. | yesterday (UTC) |
| `startUrls` | string[] | Leaderboard addresses, for example `https://www.producthunt.com/leaderboard/daily/2026/11/4`. Read in addition to the dates. | none |
| `maxResults` | integer | Most products to return across all pages. 0 uses 100. | `100` |

## Usage examples

### Three days of launches

```json
{
  "mode": "daily",
  "dates": ["2026-11-02", "2026-11-03", "2026-11-04"],
  "maxResults": 100
}
```

### One week

```json
{
  "mode": "weekly",
  "dates": ["2026-10-28"],
  "maxResults": 50
}
```

### A leaderboard address

```json
{
  "startUrls": ["https://www.producthunt.com/leaderboard/monthly/2026/10"]
}
```

## Output

Results are saved to the default dataset. Export them as JSON, CSV or Excel, or read them through the API.

Sample record:

```json
{
  "id": "1295912",
  "slug": "wanaka-studio",
  "url": "https://www.producthunt.com/products/wanaka-studio",
  "name": "Wanaka Studio",
  "tagline": "Make and publish 3D games with the first AI game engine",
  "rank": 1,
  "votes_count": 429,
  "comments_count": 106,
  "topics": ["Artificial Intelligence", "Games", "No-Code"],
  "launch_date": "2026-11-04",
  "leaderboard_date": "2026-11-04",
  "leaderboard_mode": "daily"
}
```

## Limitations

- Each leaderboard page gives the first 17 or so ranked products. The page loads further products only when a visitor scrolls, and the actor does not read those. For more products, ask for more dates, or use weekly and monthly leaderboards.
- The leaderboard does not show a long description, the product website, the makers or the hunter. Those fields are not returned.
- Votes and comments are the numbers at the time of the run.
- Dates before the site existed, or in the future, give no products.
- If the site refuses every request, the run fails and nothing is charged.

## FAQ

**Which pages does it read?**
The daily, weekly and monthly leaderboards at `producthunt.com/leaderboard`.

**How many products do I get per date?**
About 17 per leaderboard page. Three daily dates give about 50 products.

**What does a run cost?**
The start price plus the price per product, see the pricing table. A run with one date costs about 17 products plus the start event.

**What status does a run end with?**
The run status says how many products were delivered. If a date has no products, the run ends normally and says so. If the site refuses every request, the run fails and nothing is charged.

**Can I get comments or votes by user?**
No. This actor returns the leaderboard summary of each product, not the comment text or the voters.
